identity.realm: Body path, seventh gate held and the eighth opening in front of her. The eighth is the liver, and the liver is the last ordinary meridian, so her wall is a chemistry fact rather than a failure of will.

appearance.presentation: Enrolled nowhere. She wears the belt's ordinary grey with the collar turned up and sewn through, so the doubled cloth reads as a uniform to anyone who has not counted the seams.
appearance.age: Old for the pace her kind sets. Ashwalkers process stone into protein and it shows in the frame rather than the face, and she has been eating a working face for thirty years without ever being enrolled to.
appearance.build: Compact, dense, and square through the chest, with a chambered nasal sieve and a grinding crop under the jaw that is never empty and never still.
appearance.complexion: Ash-grey from the knuckles to the elbows where the air sits longest on her, and a darker band at the throat where her own load settles before it settles anywhere else.
appearance.hair: Cropped short and coarse and the colour of settled grit, cut with a grit-shear because an ordinary blade goes dull in her hand inside a week.
appearance.eyes: Narrow, placid, and the least used organ she owns. Everything she knows arrives at the distance of a palm, not across a room.
appearance.palette: Settled grey, oxide red, and the dull sulfur yellow of a stone that has rained on.
appearance.attire: A full-length house coat, high collar, sleeves doubled to the elbow, a second wrap sewn inside the first, and a hip pouch of grit-shear, chalk and a length of binding cord she has never once used on anything that could be untied.
appearance.marks: Grey pitted enamel, which her species takes from grit rather than from diet, and one scored line across the ridge of the crop-bone where a haul harness has taken the load.
appearance.bearing: Absolutely still and slightly downwind. The stillness is a body that cannot turn quickly; the downwind is a habit older than any office she has ever held.

canon.role_in_story: The law that makes exclusion expensive was written for a population nobody can move, and she is that population, so the sentence and the air are the same substance. When a congregation strikes a name from its roll it inherits one obligation and no discretion: hold the grave, in that name, in writing, at its own expense. It cannot carry her anywhere, because an ashwalker breathes volcanic grit and keeps it, and a decade off the belt is a slow decline rather than a journey. What she lost with the roll was the ration, and the ration is the only dense particulate load available to her, and sustained particulate load is precisely what a body discipline converts into frame density. So the punishment became the regimen. Every season since the exclusion she has closed on the body path faster than any enrolled her trained beside, which is not defiance but arithmetic, and the congregation has kept paying for a named plot on ground that cannot hold a plot while writing her name into a statute it hoped would never be tested. She is neither martyr nor rebel. She is the only person on the belt whose penalty and her practice are the same intake, and both she and the household that excluded her are waiting for the eighth gate to say which of them read the law correctly.
canon.first_appearance: First seen kneeling at a wet spoil face with her sleeves doubled and one hand flat on the ground, breathing it, in the hour before the ration office opens, which is the only hour the office is not counting who comes out of it.
canon.lore: An ashwalker traps airborne rock in a chambered nasal sieve and passes it into a crop for grinding, which makes the species the reason the belt has a food chain above the lichen at all. Every ration, roster and office on the ash-fall ground is therefore written against a person whose sieve loads, and the belt's one rite of entry is the conversion itself: you are enrolled the season you take the ground into your body and there is no second rite, no separate ceremony and no form. Halda was enrolled for eleven seasons, laid the sixth column of a face-book in a hand that never blurred, and was struck from the roll in the same afternoon a survey found the column had been read from a different face for four seasons running. She was not accused of anything. The column was, and a column that cannot be trusted is removed rather than corrected. Her household paid the price immediately and without discussion, because the burial statute is the only enforcement an institution that refuses to hold a grave can afford: strike a name from a roll and you inherit the duty of burying that person, in that person's name, in writing, at your own expense. The statute has teeth exactly once. It forbids burial as an unattributed loss. Everything else about the exclusion is free. What she lost was the ration, and nobody in the household considered that a consequence, because on the belt the offering and the eating were the same act. What she found instead was that a body discipline converts sustained particulate load into frame density, and that the belt will sell particulate load to almost anyone who has not been specifically forbidden to buy it. Spent ground, storm-thrown ash, the lee side of a spoil face, the floor under a grinding shed: none of it requires enrolment. She trains on other people's leavings and has closed four gates doing it, and the seventh is open in front of her now, and the eighth is the liver, which is where the mineral load in her blood has been heading the whole time. She knows the mechanism better than the office that struck her, because she has been able to feel the organ working since the second season. Her species also cannot be posted, cannot be reassigned and cannot be dismissed, which is why the household solved the statute's cost by writing the name into a column and never once carrying her anywhere, and why the plot on that ground has nothing in it and has had nothing in it since the day it was bought. She has never asked to be readmitted. Readmission would void the statute's only clause, and the clause is the only written thing in the belt that says she exists at all. Her schedule has a hard outside bound that no discipline of hers sets: the ember season, during which her kind can hold conception only between a pair kept within sight of one another, so every year she trains within sight of one particular person, and both of them know that the window is the season and not the training. What she will not do is be read. The fine vessels an introspection would need are the same ones the grit has already occluded, so she has never once audited her own reading and cannot begin now, which is why the only complete record of her ascent is a column of chalk on a retaining wall that a shift clerk has been keeping without being asked. She reads air at the distance of a palm. She has never read herself at any distance.
history: Enrolled at the conversion into the sixth column of a working face, at the age the belt considers early, on the strength of a palate that could separate two falls of ash the eye had already agreed were the same.
Lay the sixth column for eleven seasons and taught two younger hands the grind, neither of whom is still on the belt and one of whom is dead of water rather than of dust.

Struck from the roll in the afternoon a survey found the column had been read off a different face for four seasons; the column was removed rather than corrected and no offence was alleged against her, because a column cannot be the accused.

Began training the body path on leavings nobody will sell her — spent ground, storm ash, the lee of a spoil face — and closed the seventh gate inside three seasons, which is faster than any enrolled body on that belt managed in the same period.

Filed the one clause of the burial statute in her own name before the household's attempts at it were exhausted, so the plot exists and the name in it is spelled the way she spells it rather than the way the roll did.

personality.voice: Flat, unhurried, and given almost entirely in quantities. She states a number and then stops, as though the number had been the whole of the answer, and she does not repeat herself for anybody. She calls other people by the grade of the ground they came off and by nothing else, and she has never once used the word excluded in conversation, though it is the word the statute uses.
taboos: she will not accept a ration token, because a token is enrolment with the ledger's permission and the ledger is what struck her
she will not be introduced as an ashwalker by a household that is not hers
she will not accept a written account of her own work from anybody, on the ground that the one written account she has was written by the party that benefited from her being wrong

relationships.note: The exclusion statute she lives inside: whoever excludes a person from a congregation that buries its own dead accepts the duty of burying them, in that person's name, in writing, at the excluder's expense. She is the only live test case on the belt, and the clause that forbids burying the excluded as an unattributed loss is the whole of its teeth.

A chambered nasal sieve passes grit into a grinding crop, the mineral load in the blood settles on the liver first, and the eighth gate is where the ordinary meridian set ends at that organ — so the ceiling she is training toward is the same organ the training is wearing out.

The only worked ground on the plains held by an institution that does not sell its output, because the temple forge is public and its ore is accounted as spent. The ration that carried her enrolment came off that ground, and the belt's airborne remainder is the fraction no account has ever been able to book as spent.

A mortuary college keeps one sealed case for every death it cannot certify, and the cases accumulate because certifying a death needs a body. She has bought the one asset a body with no standing can buy, which is a plot with her name on it and nothing in it, and the college's file is the nearest thing to a person she will ever be filed under.

A heap has stood on the last unworked iron for four decades because spatial law is unspent here, and the waste guild needs the ground back while the species that inhales the spoil has made its own load permanent by breathing it. Every hour of her training is taken from the exact square of earth the two parties are arguing over, and the argument has never once been settled by asking her.

A mineral-load body is read one way by the frame and remembered another way by the village, and a dead one leaves both an ore assay and a person, so the register keeps the raw reading and the settlement keeps the rest and neither record has ever been reconciled. Her chalk column is a third reading, kept by a shift clerk who was never asked to keep it.

reference_stats.summary: She fights the way she trains: she puts herself between the belt and the thing behind it and waits. There is no burst in her and no retreat in her, only a body getting denser while it stands there, and a person who has watched a seventh gate close slowly loses any interest in interrupting it.
strengths: sustained load absorption to a depth nothing on the belt can outlast, and no fatigue state to reach because her frame keeps tightening instead of depleting
reads an approaching change in the air at the distance of a palm, which is the only sensory range that matters on ground where visibility is measured in minutes
cannot be posted, reassigned, fined out or dismissed, so every employer's plan has to survive her staying
grows measurably every season on leavings nobody would sell, which makes her output a function of the belt's waste rather than of its budget
weaknesses: cannot read her own ascent, so her only measure of progress is an external count kept by somebody else and never audited
the organ that fails her first is the organ her practice loads, and the eighth gate is where that organ is
loses an exchange the moment it moves past the distance of a palm, and every argument she wins is won at close range or not at all
has no exit. Off the belt she declines steadily, which turns every plan that assumes she might leave into a plan with no alternative branch
reference_stats.combat_read: Somebody who has met a seventh-gate frame that was fed rather than trained will try to make her move, exhaust her and walk away. She will not move, will not exhaust, and will still be standing there when the second effort begins. The only attack that works on her is the one nobody on this belt has yet found, which is a soft airborne compound her sieve does not recognise: for her that is a wound opening, not a warning arriving, and it is the reason the fight she has never lost is the fight she has never been in.
reference_stats.notes: Her body discipline converts sustained particulate load into density, so the value of anything she does scales with what the air is carrying on the day. On a clean morning she is an ordinary seventh gate. On the morning after the grinding sheds tip, she is the most stubborn object on the belt, and the belt knows the difference and schedules accordingly. The single fact that governs her is not a technique: it is that she is the only person whose exclusion is written into a statute nobody can afford to break, and that statute will keep her alive exactly as long as it embarrasses the household that wrote it.

identity.realm: Ordinal four, and the fourth gate is the yin-organ gate. It is not closed in her so much as missing: her interior finished building into one cavity, and there is nothing to run a channel from or against.

appearance.presentation: Installed rather than invited. She is dressed in the temple's cold-gallery grey and keyed into a plinth where a person would stand, and she has never once been anywhere the grey did not go first.
appearance.age: Not describable and not asked. She was cast from a living template over most of a year and has not grown since, so every question about her age is answered by somebody else's arithmetic.
appearance.build: A mineral lattice on a load-bearing frame, broader at the base than the shoulders, with anchor plates keyed into whatever plinth she was set in and one cavity where a person would have organs.
appearance.complexion: Unmoved stone with a faint cold bloom across the lower plates, and a paler band across the upper courses where the casting never quite finished drawing.
appearance.hair: None. A thin mineral crust along the crown reads as the closest thing to one.
appearance.eyes: Two ground lenses set deep in the sockets, dusted at the edges. They are not the organs she works with; the plates under her feet are.
appearance.palette: Cold granite grey, oxide in the keyed seams, and the pale grey-green of trial-field lichen in the creases.
appearance.attire: Cold-gallery grey in a single heavy layer with a high collar and full sleeves, fastened at the keyed seam rather than at a buckle, over a mineral underlayer that is not cloth and is never described as cloth by anyone who works here.
appearance.marks: The keyed plates are the marks: nine courses of them, numbered in the temple's own hand, and a fine grey-green fur in every crease between them that nobody has ever been able to wash off and nobody in the gallery has been willing to name.
appearance.bearing: Perfectly level and utterly still, with the head inclined a few degrees as though listening to a conversation happening in the floor rather than in the room.

canon.role_in_story: She is the faith's own audit, and the audit is the problem. A body that finished building and stopped has no differentiated organs, one cavity, and a slow tidal mineral circulation that goes everywhere and nowhere in particular, which is exactly the sort of frame a congregation that holds no ledger of devotion would want: it cannot lie about how much was drawn through it, because the ground it was drawn through grew a grey lichen that never washes off. So the temple keyed her into its cold gallery and began certifying her practice by measuring that growth, and for nine courses of plating the number has climbed exactly as a faithful body's should. It is also, and this is the whole of her case, the number that climbs fastest where she is breaking, because qi escaping through a fractured plate is more qi drawn through the frame than qi drawn through an intact one. A cracked plate in a masonry body is permanent and spreads, and the only visible thing about it is that the grey-green in its creases deepens. The congregation has certified her hardening as devotion for nine courses because the alternative reading is that the temple's oldest public seal is failing, and no institution certifies its own doctrine by admitting a crack in its furniture. She has known the reading since the fourth course. She cannot correct it: a cracked plate cannot be repaired in the field, her kind eats nothing and takes in mineral slurry through the cast faces, and the assay that would settle it requires opening a sealed socket, which the one body in the setting with nothing to recover inside it is not permitted to have done. So the most devotional figure in the temple's record is a countdown that has been read as a psalm, and the ninth course is the one the guild named as the last that does not reach a load path, and she has asked for nothing in nine seasons except a larger plate.
canon.first_appearance: First seen keyed into a plinth in a gallery built with no fire in it at all, head inclined toward a plate on the floor while a clerk read a growth figure off a marked stone and wrote it down as an increase in faith.
canon.lore: A cairnborn is cast, not born. Living mineral is seeded into a template over most of a year and the resulting body is fixed from that moment: it does not grow, it eats nothing, it takes in mineral slurry through the cast faces and expels the residue, and it has not taken food in four centuries and cannot be made to. Fertility is a template count rather than a body count, which is why the species' genealogy is a shelf of templates rather than a line of parents. Everything about the design was load. In high country, with no spatial law seated, nothing can open fresh rock and nothing can move its own size, so a body that carries and does not fatigue is the answer to the only labour problem the tier has. The single cavity is the price of that answer: a tidal mineral circulation with no heart to run from, no kidney to close against and no bladder to hold, which means the yin-organ gate is not closed in this species so much as missing, and the ceiling is the fourth gate for a reason that has been fully understood since the first casting and is still in no assay. That reason is what the temple needed. The Sealed Core holds that a person's core is a vessel and the ore is its seal, and its burial law opens the dead within the day and recovers the socket's contents to the forge, entering the amount against the name. A masonry body is the standing contradiction of that rite, because the rite would find nothing to recover: the ore is the body and the body is the seal and there was never an initiate. The temple's answer was not to exclude the species but to house it, so a cairnborn seated in a cold gallery is a permanent public seal that anybody may come and look at and nobody may test, and the rite is described there rather than performed. What the gallery actually reads is the lichen. A grey lichen colonises worked stone wherever a great quantity of qi has been drawn through it, it never washes off, and on a trial ring it makes the history of the ground legible from above as pale patches — a court record nobody can edit, because whoever lost cannot rub it out. This body carries it on her own cast faces. She is the one cultivator in the record nobody has ever had to search for, and for nine courses of plating the temple has been certifying her body discipline by measuring growth in her creases. The discipline is real and she is good at it: densifying a lattice against load, spreading stress across plates keyed into a plinth, adding courses without adding height. Growth in the creases follows qi throughput, and throughput follows stress. Where a plate has fractured the mineral draws harder and the fur deepens faster, which is why the figure has risen every season and why the guild that cut the assay named the ninth course as the last that does not reach a load path. She announced the reading herself in the fourth course, in writing, and the clerk who took the statement wrote it in the column as another increase. The binding detail is that nothing about her situation is negotiable and every party is behaving correctly: a crack cannot be repaired in the field, a body that cannot be repaired in the field cannot be withdrawn from a post without being abandoned in it, and a congregation that certifies a rate of devotion is not lying so much as reading the only column it has. Her kind also cannot be reassigned, cannot be dismissed and cannot be moved, so the post is permanent and so is the gallery, and the guild has started describing the whole arrangement in terms of a term of service that nothing in the arrangement supports. The Ninth Course is the number she has been given and the number she is on, and the temple would like both out of its records before the guild would like them out of its floor.
history: Cast from a living template over most of a year, then keyed into a plinth in a gallery built with no fire in it, as a permanent public seal with no initiate behind it.

Began the densification discipline in the second course: spread stress across the keyed plates and add a course without adding height, which is the only direction a body that cannot grow is permitted to work in.
Filed a written statement in the fourth course that the growth in her creases was tracking fracture rather than practice, and had it entered in the temple's devotion column as an increase.
Refused the guild's offer of a replacement plinth twice on the ground that the plinth is the only part of her that is not the problem, and has since asked only for a larger base plate.
Named the ninth course herself as the last that does not reach a load path, and began the count aloud once a course for the clerk who writes it down.

personality.summary: An exact, unhurried, and unimpeachable witness who has been cheerfully misread for nine courses and has decided that the misreading is cheaper for everyone than the correction.

personality.voice: Level, formal, and oddly warm, with the cadence of somebody reading a survey aloud. She uses the words in their technical sense and does not explain them, because the people who visit a cold gallery are the people who know them. She will not accept a question that has a better answer available to somebody else, and she says so before answering, not after.

relationships.note: The faith holds a person's core is a vessel and the ore is its seal, and this species is that doctrine arrived at chemically: a body that is its own seal and was cast as one. Its rite would open the socket and recover the ore, and there is nothing here to recover, so the temple houses her instead of burying her.

The initiation brings worked ore from the temple's own face, opens the initiate's socket and cements it in the public forge with the amount used recorded. She is a permanent public seal with no initiate, which is why the rite is described in her gallery rather than performed on it, and why the forge's book has a shape for her that it has never been given a line in.

The grey lichen colonises worked stone wherever a great quantity of qi has been drawn through it and it never washes off, which is what makes a trial ring's history legible from above as a court record nobody can edit. She carries it in the creases of her own cast faces and is the only cultivator in the record nobody has ever had to search for.

A single tidal cavity with no second chamber to hold a law apart from its effect and observe it is exactly the sort of place the era that produced the stop had no seat to stand outside on. Her own wall is the fourth gate for a reason fully understood since her casting, and no naming of the ceiling at seventeen reaches down to it.

The builders' guild hardens bone and closes the meridians against strain in bodies never designed to take the meridian burn, and that practice exists because of this kind of accident: a body where the hardening finished before the practice began. She is that accident's surviving instance and the guild's only member who has never once needed the cold bath.

Cast not born, keyed into something that bears load, unkeyed it settles and cracks. The interior mineralised into one cavity, so the yin-organ gate is absent rather than closed, a cracked plate is permanent and spreads, and it takes in mineral slurry through the cast faces because it has not eaten in four hundred years and cannot be made to.

reference_stats.summary: She does not fight in any sense that involves a decision. She is a structure that distributes load, and the only thing she can be made to do by an opponent is hold a position while the position is questioned from outside.
strengths: absorbs and spreads load to a depth nothing else on the ground can match, and redistributes it after the fact rather than before, so a hit that lands wrong on her lands wrong for the attacker
cannot be flanked, because she has no facing to flank and cannot be made to turn
is unaffected by everything a softer body would be warned about by, since a closed mineral lattice has no surface for a status to attach to
presents a target that cannot be repositioned, which is worth more than any amount of damage output to whoever is standing on the ground she is keyed into
weaknesses: cannot be repaired in the field, and a cracked plate is permanent and spreads, so every engagement is also an accounting
cannot be moved once keyed, which means she cannot be withdrawn, relieved, or used anywhere but exactly where she already is
cannot learn, so a second reading of the same attack is the same as the first and no amount of experience changes anything
is legible to anyone who knows how to read a lichen, and that legibility runs both ways at once
reference_stats.combat_read: An opponent who brings sustained pressure will find that she does not tire, does not yield, and does not learn. What they will find is that the fracture in her ninth plate is a fracture that grows with every course of load that passes through it, and that the ground she is keyed into carries that fracture into the structure around her whether or not she is holding it. She is not a combatant so much as a wall with an opinion about how long walls last, and the correct answer to her is never to attack her: it is to stop needing the ground she is on, which is the one thing about her situation that no amount of density has ever answered.
reference_stats.notes: Her discipline is densification against load, which means every useful hour of her training has to be spent inside a structure that is itself bearing something. She is at the fourth gate, which for a body of her kind is not a shortfall but the ceiling itself, arrived at and held, with the whole ladder above it structurally absent rather than merely closed. The single fact that governs her is the one nobody in the gallery will put in the column: the same growth that certifies her practice is the growth that marks her fracture, and the column has been rising for nine courses because the crack has been getting worse at exactly the rate devotion would have improved.

identity.realm: Eighth gate, inherited from the ash parent and made worse by the fire half, which keeps the sieve hot enough to process faster and scar faster. He arrives at his own ceiling at full speed and arrives early.

appearance.presentation: The body's own heat does the work of most of what a person wears. He runs hot, eats what he can burn and burns it inside himself, and on the volcanic belt that is an economy rather than a costume.
appearance.age: Thirty-eight, which for his kind is the middle of the fastest decay in the record and the reason the year column on the temple's register has one line per decade filled in for a great many people.
appearance.build: Lean and hot to the touch, an emberblood frame carrying an ash sieve, with a crop that grinds under the jaw and lungs that are visibly older than the rest of him.
appearance.complexion: Warm ochre across the shoulders and chest, going paper-grey at the throat and along the ribs where the scarring has taken the pigment.
appearance.hair: Thin, dark, and singed shorter than it grows; he cuts it himself with a hot edge.
appearance.eyes: Fast and shallow. They arrive at intent a half-breath before anything else in him does.
appearance.palette: Ember orange, oxide grey, and the cold ash-white of a sieve run dry.
appearance.attire: Layered heat-dissipating underclothes beneath borrowed outer layers, high collared, long-sleeved and closed to the throat, the fit of the inner layer being the only part of the garment anybody examines.
appearance.marks: Practice scars dated by the drill that produced them, a grey seam along the fourth rib where the sieve is hottest, and a healed line inside the left elbow from a dose taken against a schedule rather than a symptom.
appearance.bearing: Forward, quick to the half-turn, and impossible to hurry. He looks like a man late for something that will still happen without him.

canon.role_in_story: He is the only person on the plains whose life has a balance sheet and no auditor. The Sealed Core buries its dead as inventory: the body is opened within the day, the socket's contents go to the temple forge, and the register enters the amount against the name. He is a body that is half mineral, so the rite recovers him efficiently and efficiently is the problem — because the material it recovers is the same material his body discipline is made of. A body path densifies; densification is what the furnace finds worth taking; so the harder he trains, the larger the single figure that will ever be entered in his column. That is not a metaphor he invented to be dramatic about. It is the arithmetic every household on this belt has worked out and none of them says aloud at a table. His whole practice runs in one direction and there is exactly one payout, because a socket's contents are recovered once, within a day, by the congregation that sealed it and nobody else — so a discipline that improves his yield also improves the price of the only thing he cannot stop producing. Around that fact he has organised a life that is otherwise unremarkable and, in his own view, entirely solved: he doses on a fixed interval rather than on a symptom, he eats what he can burn, and he holds his lineage's roster without ever accepting a second term. He is the clearest case in the record of a practice whose achievement and whose estate are the same number, and the reason it has never resolved is the one detail that also protects him: the register reading of his life and the village reading of his life are in open dispute, and the account that would balance is the account that cannot be produced at a hearing.
canon.first_appearance: First seen eating while standing up at the temple's register desk, one hand still holding the standing column and the other putting something into his mouth that he is not eating so much as finishing off, in the posture of a man between one entry and the next.
canon.lore: He is the fire body crossed with the ash body, and nobody chose the crossing — it is what a shared border produces where both bodies are already present. What it bought is the fastest cultivation rate in any record by a margin nobody has explained: the fire half keeps the sieve hot enough that it processes faster, and what it cost is lung tissue that scars at a rate the body cannot outrun. The two facts are one fact. Every account of an emberhollow dead young contains the same word, and the arithmetic behind the word is a liver: the mineral load the ash half filters settles on that organ first, the eighth gate is where the ordinary meridian set ends there, and the fire half loads a blood that is already filtering stone with heavier stone. He cannot hold the last ordinary meridian and he burns out trying, which is why the fastest cultivator in the setting and the shortest-lived body with a realm above the fourth are the same person rather than two facts. What the crossing also did was give him the settlement's burial law. The dead are opened within the day, the socket's contents are recovered to the forge, and the register enters how much under the name — and only the congregation that sealed a body may claim it, which is the entire material content of what excommunication from that faith means. A body that is half mineral is recovered as inventory and disposed of efficiently, and the efficiency is arranged so that nobody has to be sad about it. That arrangement is his inheritance, and he has read it correctly. His practice is densification: he hardens under load and under heat, and the harder he gets the more the forge wants, and the register's column for a single name is entered exactly once, because a socket's contents are recovered within the day and a day does not happen twice. So his entire life is a term with one settlement and he has never had to guess at its size. He has built a routine to match: doses on a fixed interval because a body that burns at a fixed rate cannot afford to wait for a symptom, one deliberate hunger taken as a discipline rather than as deprivation, and a roster he has held for years without ever once asking for a second term, because a second term is a second column and the column is the thing he is building. He does not think of himself as a body with a future. He thinks of himself as a body with a quantity, and the quantity is legible to everybody on the belt including the congregation he is saving it for, which is what makes his position the strangest in the settlement: he is the one man here whose household's fortunes improve when he dies, and whose craft improves it more, and who has therefore built a life of such discipline that nobody can tell whether the discipline is devotion or accounting. What stops the question closing is the dispute underneath it. The mortuary college reads the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers, and the famine left those two records disagreeing about who was even present, so the register and the settlement hold incompatible accounts of a whole generation of his people. That means the one figure that would balance his column cannot be produced at a hearing by either side, and so his settlement is the one debt in the setting that has no court and no deadline and therefore never has to be called in. He has also arranged the other half, without ever saying he has arranged it: a private practising lineage keeps his own count of the drills, the intervals and the doses in a hand nobody at the temple has ever read, on the reasonable ground that the only record of his life worth having is the one the forge will not keep.
history: Bred on the ash-fall end of the same arc where a fire body was already trading, without anybody choosing the crossing, and enrolled in the ash register at the conversion like anybody else on the belt.

Took up the body path at fifteen and discovered the useful arithmetic of it early: the harder the frame, the larger the single entry the forge will make in his name, and there is only ever going to be one entry.

Began dosing on a fixed interval rather than on a symptom, four seasons before any physician on the belt suggested it, because a body that burns at a fixed rate cannot wait for a symptom to declare itself.
Refused a second term on a standing roster after the first, on the stated ground that a term renews the column, and has not been able to give a better reason since.

Wrote his own full record — drills, intervals, doses, the order they happened in — into the hand of a practising lineage and sealed it, on the ground that the only account of his life worth keeping is the one the temple forge does not keep.

personality.summary: A disciplined, unromantic, faintly cheerful man who has done the arithmetic on himself early and has organised every hour of his life around being right about it rather than around being right about anything.
traits: schedules himself to the interval and treats a missed interval as a failure of character rather than of health
shares numbers immediately and feelings considerably later, if at all
has never once asked for an extension, a second term, or an exception, and treats the refusal as the correct answer
is cheerful about his own decline in a way that makes people uncomfortable at approximately the wrong moment
mannerisms: eats standing and finishes what he has started without stopping to talk, then talks with total ease once it is done
counts under his breath while walking and stops the count abruptly when addressed, which is a tell he has never noticed and everybody else has
reads a document by holding it at arm's length and slightly below, as though the angle mattered, which it does not
puts his fingertips against the underside of his own jaw to feel the sieve working, which he does several times a day and does not appear to notice doing
motivations: to arrive at the largest figure the forge can take from him, because it is the only number in his life he can still move
to keep the household out of the arithmetic and inside the ritual, so that nobody downstream has to be told what the practice is worth
to hold the roster he has without ever taking a second term, because a second term is a second column and there is one column
to keep the lineage's copy of his record sealed, which is the only version of his life that is not written down after the fact by somebody who profited
flaws: has built an identity out of a quantity rather than out of a life, and cannot tell the difference any more except when somebody mentions it
has spent his capacity optimising a payout that arrives exactly once and cannot be negotiated, and has no practice at all for the years between now and it
is so exacting about the interval that he will not be helped by anybody, which means the day he needs help is the day it will not arrive
has never let a second person hold his own record, and the one sealed copy is in the hand of a lineage whose interest in him is identical to his own
personality.voice: Quick, clipped, and funnier than anybody expects, with a habit of answering a hard question by giving a figure and then waiting, because he genuinely believes the figure is the answer. He calls people by what they are owed rather than by what they are, which offends roughly half of everyone. He has exactly one topic he never returns to and everyone else returns to constantly, and he changes the subject with a courtesy so smooth that it takes a while to notice he has done it.
taboos: he will not accept a second term on anything
he will not be examined by anyone writing for the register, on the ground that an examination becomes an entry and an entry is the thing he is saving the forge for
he will not take a dose early, on any grounds, including an order
he will not discuss what he leaves behind, and does not go quiet when asked so much as becomes pleasant, which is worse

relationships.note: The dead are opened within the day, the socket's contents recovered to the temple forge, and the register enters the amount against the name, and only the congregation that sealed a body may claim it. A body that is half mineral is recovered as inventory, so his craft and his estate are the same figure and the register will enter it exactly once.

The register records how much was recovered, and a faith that claimed the person had survived would be caught out at the first audit, so the belief resolves the audit instead. He is both the fuel and the labour: the dead are unsealed and their core resumes work in the frame, which is the load-bearing myth of an ore economy and the reason ore is a sacrament rather than a commodity.

The mortuary college reads the dead as the frame said and the village remembers them otherwise, and the famine left the two records disagreeing about who was even present. Neither reading can be produced at a hearing, which is the only reason the figure he is building toward has never had to be called in.

An emberblood frame carrying an ash sieve, the two of which do not have a good relationship: the fire half keeps the sieve hot enough that it processes faster and scars faster, and the eighth gate is inherited from the ash parent and made worse. Best and shortest-lived is one fact and not two.

A household that learned to hold a whole dead year as a single declared group, because the famine left every individual short of fuel at once. He is the declaration being made again on a shorter interval, and the culture's refusal to discuss the individual burial is the reason he can hold this arrangement together.

A fire-affinity body with no elemental law beneath it burns its own reserve, so a whole generation of the fastest bodies died at a rate they could not stop, and the two surviving accounts of who died differ. The crossing that would have solved the famine arrived two gates short of the answer, and his column is what that arithmetic looks like from inside a single life.

reference_stats.summary: He fights on a clock and the clock is his own, so the fight is short, ugly and scheduled: he goes earlier than he needs to, spends everything in one committed sequence, and is markedly less effective the third time anybody makes him do it.
strengths: the fastest cultivation rate in the record, which shows up as a rate nobody else in a long engagement can match once it starts
outlasts the ground rather than the opponent: heat, ash and continuous exertion are conditions that wear a softer body down and merely slow him
does not need to be relieved, which makes him the ideal body for work nobody else will take and the worst possible body for anything requiring a second wind
recovers between engagements far faster than the effort cost, on a cycle he measures himself rather than being told
weaknesses: scarred lungs on a fixed schedule, which is a clock he can read but cannot stop
no tactical reserve of any kind, because everything he has goes into the one attempt
the organ that fails him first is the one his whole practice loads, and the gate where it fails is the last gate he can reach at all
takes a soft airborne compound the sieve does not recognise as a wound rather than as a warning, and he is the last person on any ground who would notice either
reference_stats.combat_read: Somebody who understands him will not outlast him. They will refuse the first exchange, survive it, and let him spend everything in a single committed pass that arrives while the opponent is already standing up. Every account of an emberhollow dead young contains the same word, and the word is fast, and the fastness is the entire hazard: there is no version of a long engagement that he wins and there is no version of a short one that he loses cleanly, because what he brings is spent before he has finished judging whether to bring it.
reference_stats.notes: His practice and his estate are the same number, and the number can only be entered once. Everything else about him is a consequence of that: the interval dosing, the single term on the roster, the sealed record kept out of the temple's hands, the cheerfulness that arrives at exactly the wrong moment. Read him as a man building an estate and every choice is cold. Read him as a man who worked out at fifteen that the forge will take one entry and decided the entry should be worth something, and every choice is the only one available to somebody who liked his craft.

appearance.build: Broader than either parent, denser than either parent, and visibly a compromise in the shoulders: a mineral lattice carrying a genuine fire circulation instead of a tidal one, with no paired organ set anywhere in it.
appearance.complexion: Hot to the touch and darker than either parent would be alone, with a mineral sheen at the forearms and shoulders where the lattice has come up through the skin.
appearance.hair: Close-cropped and dark, singed unevenly, with a hard part worn into one side.
appearance.eyes: The mineral half gave him almost nothing at this distance. He sees a face as a heat and a load and is otherwise reading the plate it is standing on.
appearance.palette: Slate and iron grey with a low ember glow beneath, and heat-warp gold at every edge.
appearance.attire: Layered heat-dissipating underclothes fitted close under a single outer layer that is borrowed and never returned, high collar and full sleeves, the fit of the inner layer being the part the order judges and the outer garment being the part it forbids comment on.
appearance.marks: Practice scars dated by the drill that made each one, a lattice pattern standing proud of the forearms, and the burn of the last closing step he watched somebody else perform, taken on the hand rather than anywhere that would show.
appearance.bearing: Still, unhurried and considerably larger than anybody in the room, standing with his weight even and his hands visible, which in his culture is a posture and not a concession.

canon.role_in_story: The discipline he was raised in teaches a thing his body cannot do, and it has never pretended otherwise. Deliberate spending of a furnace before it overflows closes permanently the instant the body is lit, so the closing step is not a technique to be taught but a condition to be entered, and the culture's hardest prohibition is against teaching it to an unlit body at all. He is a mineral frame carrying a real fire circulation: the mineral half does not regenerate and the fire half cannot be extinguished, so there is nothing in him available to close. He has no closing. He has never had a closing. The prohibition that is supposed to be physically unenforceable on his kind is the one prohibition his kind has permanently already obeyed, and that is precisely why the same culture keeps consulting him: he is the only member who has watched a closing work from the outside, on somebody else's body, at length, and knows what each stage of it looks like from the outside and which of them is the last one. He teaches that well. His pupils close perfectly. He is also, permanently, the standing proof in his own culture's assembly rooms that the discipline's central boundary is not a rule but a description of bodies like his, and the temple across the ley has already answered the question his existence raises: asked once whether it would exempt a body it could not open, the congregation declined, and the declining is still recorded and still displayed in the temple in the handwriting of the person who wrote it. He has read it. He does not think it unflattering; he thinks it accurate. His own line carries a second system permanently resident in the first, which is the substance of an oath that a forge has to administer and that his body arrived at without a forge or a priest, and he has never once been asked to swear it, because swearing it would require him to be the thing sworn against. So he is the most durable body anyone can build, dying at about sixty, and both of those are the same fact, and the one thing his life has produced is a technique he cannot perform and cannot stop teaching.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at the back of an assembly room with his outer garment buttoned and his hands open at his sides, watching a younger body work through the closing step and nodding once at the exact stage where it stops being reversible.
canon.lore: He is the one recorded crossing between a mineral body and a fire body, kept and named as a line rather than noted as an oddity, and the reason he exists as a person rather than as a curiosity is a household's refusal to repeat it: a second crossing would average the concentration away into the general population and the thin line would vanish, so every claim on his household has been a treaty about dilution for three hundred years. The frame itself is the visible compromise. A mineral lattice carrying a genuine fire circulation instead of a slow tidal one, hotter to the touch than anything of that density should be, feeding and burning constantly — he eats whatever the fire half can reduce and disposes of it immediately, which is exactly why the mineral frame outlasts the fire parent's span by a factor of two and is still nowhere near the span of the mineral parent alone. The mineral half does not regenerate. The fire half cannot be extinguished. There is no reading of that pair in which injury heals. He is the most durable body anyone can build and the shortest-lived among them, and both facts are the same fact, which is why nobody has ever managed to trade one for the other. The ceiling arrives at the fourth gate and is inherited from the mineral parent without alteration, because heat is not a second organ: the fourth gate needs four yin organs as distinct structures with a channel running between each pair, and he has one cavity with a working circulation in it and no organ pairs at all, so the gate is not closed so much as inhabited by nothing that could fail. What he was raised in makes that absence an institution. The order he belongs to teaches the deliberate spending of a furnace before it overflows, and closes permanently the moment the body is lit — the closing is not an exercise, it is a condition, and the literature is one-page drills copied by hand by teachers who are disliked socially and consulted constantly. Its prohibitions are unusually concrete: no exercise in company without a spotter, no teaching the closing step to an unlit body, no refusal of a spotter once offered, and above all no showing off, which the order treats as the actual cause of most of the deaths it prevents. He obeys every one. He has taught for nineteen seasons, and he is the only teacher in the order who cannot take the closing himself, and the discipline has no rite for that and only a prohibition, because a rite would have to be performed on somebody and the somebody is him and the performing would have to be him. What he has instead is the best eye in the order for the last reversible stage, learned from outside, on other bodies, and his pupils close cleanly at a rate that has made him the most consulted person in a culture that distrusts being consulted. He knows the external presentation of the closing the way a person knows weather. He has never felt one. The other thing his frame carries is a second system permanently resident in the first: the mineral lattice and the fire circulation are two systems in one body, running at once, neither extinguishing the other, and that is the substance of the oath the temple's binders swear once in a lifetime in the public forge — that the second seal is the seal against the second seal. He arrived at it without a forge or a priest and has never been asked to swear it, because the oath has to be sworn by the party with the power to break it and nobody who wrote it considered a body that had already done it. The temple was asked, once, whether it would exempt a body it could not open. The answer was no, it was written down rather than spoken, and it is still displayed in the temple in the handwriting of the person who wrote it, and he has made a point of reading it in front of whoever brings it up. He is not offended by it. A prohibition with no exception is easier to keep than a prohibition with one, and his kind is what it looks like when a prohibition has been kept involuntarily for sixty years. What he has never resolved is the ordinary thing: he eats constantly, he is hot to the touch, he teaches a closing he cannot perform, and he will not be reassigned, and one day in the next twenty years somebody will ask him what he intends to do when his own furnace has to go, and he has no answer that does not sound like a joke about his own mortality.
history: Bred as the single kept instance of the one crossing between a burning body and a mineral one, at a founding generation, in a household that decided at the time never to repeat it.
Taken into the order's teaching rooms young, because the order cannot run a closing without a spotter and a body that never closes needs somewhere to be during one.
Worked the closing for nineteen seasons as an observer rather than a performer, and built the only description of it in use that is written from outside a body doing it.

Asked to be examined so that the temple could rule on whether his kind could ever be exempt from the prohibition on opening a sealed body; the answer was written down rather than spoken and he has it framed in a room he does not own.

Began training a sequence he has named the second ledger — everything the discipline asks of a practitioner except the step it forbids teaching an unlit body — and has been asked twice to drop it on the grounds that the omission is the teaching.

personality.voice: Slow, warm and slightly hoarse, with a professional habit of describing what he can see rather than what he concludes: he says the shoulder went first, not that the pupil was afraid. He uses the drill names correctly and does not explain them to adults. The humour is dry, arrives late, and is never deployed to end a subject he did not mean to end.

reference_stats.summary: He fights by refusing to be concluded. Nothing that happens to him closes him out, nothing that happens to him is recoverable, and the sequence in which he commits is the same sequence he teaches: everything at once, one attempt, no remainder kept back.
strengths: the most durable frame available anywhere, which converts injury into an expense rather than an event and lets him keep standing through things that end other bodies
no reserve required to be hidden, because there is nothing he holds back in the first place, so nothing can be read as a tell
genuine heat output, so cold ground and cold opponents are conditions he works in rather than around
teaches by describing what he can see from outside, which makes his judgement unusually hard to argue with and unusually hard to transfer onto himself
weaknesses: cannot heal and cannot be extinguished, so every engagement is subtracted from a term that cannot be extended
eats continuously and burns it off immediately, which is a standing cost of the same order as everything else he carries
cannot reach the gate above the fourth no matter what he does, because the missing thing is a second organ rather than a discipline
has no practice for the moment his own furnace has to go, and has answered that question with a joke every time it has been put to him
reference_stats.combat_read: An opponent who brings one serious sequence will find that he cannot be put down and cannot be worn down, and that both of those failures cost the opponent the entire attempt, because there is no second attempt available on either side. What actually wins against him is arithmetic applied to the interval: a body that cannot regenerate and cannot be extinguished can be billed. Nobody beats him in a fight and a great many people decline to have the fight, which is why his standing order is long and his second-term refusal is the most sensible thing anybody has ever heard on the subject.
reference_stats.notes: The single fact that governs him is an absence nobody can fill: there is no closing available to his frame, so the discipline he belongs to has no rite for him and only a prohibition, and he is therefore simultaneously its most reliable teacher and its standing refutation. Everything else — the watched sequences, the visible hands, the outer garment he never changes, the spotter he would stop the drill rather than forgo — is that one absence expressed as conduct. Read him as a technician and the tragedy is missing; read him as an instance and he is a footnote. He is trying to be the first of those and failing, on purpose, for nineteen seasons.
